We need to analyze method normalizeMetaSchemaUri(String u). It does:

try {
    URI uri = new URI(u);
    URI newUri = new URI("https", uri.getUserInfo(), uri.getHost(), uri.getPort(), uri.getPath(), null, null);
    return newUri.toString();
} catch (URISyntaxException e) {
    throw new JsonSchemaException("Wrong MetaSchema URI: " + u);
}

Potential exception scenarios:

- URISyntaxException thrown by new URI(u) for invalid syntax => wrapped in JsonSchemaException.
- NullPointerException if u is null (new URI(null) throws NullPointerException? Actually URI(String) throws NullPointerException if str is null). Not caught, propagates.
- Also possible IllegalArgumentException from new URI("https", ...) if components are invalid (e.g., host null but path not starting with '/'), but that is unlikely? Actually URI constructor may throw NullPointerException for scheme null, IllegalArgumentException for illegal characters. Could cause URISyntaxException? No, it throws URISyntaxException only for parsing strings, but constructors may throw IllegalArgumentException. In this method, they pass components individually; if any component is invalid (e.g., host contains illegal characters) it may throw IllegalArgumentException. That is not caught; test should capture.

Examples: host contains space (invalid) leading to IllegalArgumentException.

Also port negative? new URI may accept -1 for unspecified; but passing -1 is fine. But passing port out of range maybe IllegalArgumentException. Actually URI constructor validates port range (0-65535) else IllegalArgumentException.

Thus we need test cases for IllegalArgumentException scenario.

Also test for when uri.getHost() returns null (e.g., relative URI) leading to new URI with null host but path maybe not null; that is allowed. But maybe if both host and path are null leads to something? Not exception.

Edge: userInfo containing illegal characters? Might cause IllegalArgumentException.

Thus we need to add new test groups for exception scenarios not covered: IllegalArgumentException, maybe NullPointerException (already covered), maybe URISyntaxException already covered.

Existing test cases include NullPointerException case, and URISyntaxException cases.

Missing: IllegalArgumentException due to invalid host, userInfo, or path characters.

Also maybe scenario where scheme is null? Not applicable.

Thus create new group: "normalizeMetaSchemaUri - illegal argument handling". Cases:

1. Input with host containing space: "http://exa mple.com/path". Expect IllegalArgumentException.

2. Input with userInfo containing illegal character like '@' inside? Actually userInfo can contain any characters except maybe ':', but colon is allowed? Might be fine. Use "http://user:pa ss@example.com". Space in userInfo leads to IllegalArgumentException.

3. Input with path containing illegal character like control char? Use "http://example.com/pa^th". '^' maybe allowed? Actually '^' is allowed in path? Not sure. Use "http://example.com/<>". That may cause IllegalArgumentException.

Check Java URI constructor: IllegalArgumentException if any component contains illegal characters. For example, space not allowed. So use "http://example.com/invalid path". Expect IllegalArgumentException.

Thus add test cases expecting IllegalArgumentException.

Make sure not duplicate existing cases.

Also maybe scenario where port is negative? "http://example.com:-1". That would cause IllegalArgumentException.

Add that.

Thus produce JSON array with new group plus maybe keep existing groups? The instruction: "Follow existing test case structure, Avoid duplication and create new test cases for uncovered exception scenarios". So we output only new test cases (uncovered). Could also include all groups? It says return test cases in JSON format. Probably only new cases.

Thus output array with one group "normalizeMetaSchemaUri - illegal argument handling" and cases.
